aiOverview.content: Barack Obama, the 44th U.S. President (2009–2017), focused on economic recovery from the 2008 recession, passing the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare), and major foreign policy shifts, including authorized the mission that killed Osama bin Laden and withdrawing troops from Iraq and Afghanistan. He also legalized same-sex marriage, implemented environmental regulations, and appointed two Supreme Court Justices. Key actions from his administration include: Healthcare & Social Policy: Signed the Affordable Care Act (2010), which expanded insurance coverage, protected pre-existing conditions, and allowed young adults to stay on parents' plans until age 26. He supported the Supreme Court decision legalizing same-sex marriage. Economic Reform: Pushed the $800 billion American Recovery and Reinvestment Act to stimulate the economy following the 2008 financial crisis. He signed the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act to regulate financial institutions. Foreign Policy & Security: Authorized the 2011 raid that killed Osama bin Laden. He brokered the Iran nuclear deal, restored diplomatic relations with Cuba, and signed the New START treaty with Russia. Environmental & Domestic Action: Implemented the Climate Action Plan to cut carbon emissions and vetoed the Keystone XL Pipeline. He appointed Sonia Sotomayor and Elena Kagan to the Supreme Court. Education & Rights: Signed the Lilly Ledbetter Fair Pay Act to reduce gender pay gaps. He enacted the Post-9/11 GI Bill to help veterans afford college.
